hints: Look at the functional group in all four structures and recall what type of compound reacts with hot aqueous NaOH by hydrolysis.
For each ester, focus only on the C=O side (the acyl group), as this becomes the carboxylate and then the acid after acidification.
List the acid from each of the four esters and notice which one is repeated, leaving you with three distinct organic acids in total.
walkthrough:
**Recognise the reaction as ester hydrolysis**

All four compounds contain the ester link, $\text{-COO-}$. With hot aqueous $\text{NaOH}$ they undergo alkaline hydrolysis (saponification).

$$\text{RCOOR' + NaOH} \rightarrow \text{RCOO}^{-}\text{Na}^{+} + \text{R'OH}$$

After acidification, $\text{RCOO}^{-}$ becomes the carboxylic acid $\text{RCOOH}$. The alcohol $\text{R'OH}$ does not become an acid.

**Identify the acid part of each ester**

Remember, the acid comes from the $\text{R-C=O}$ side, not the $\text{-O-R'}$ side.

Top left: $\text{CH}_{3}\text{CH}_{2}\text{CH}_{2}\text{COOCH}_{2}\text{CH}_{3}$ is ethyl butanoate, so acid part is $\text{CH}_{3}\text{CH}_{2}\text{CH}_{2}\text{CO-}$ which gives butanoic acid.

Top right: $\text{HCOOCH}_{2}\text{CH}_{3}$ is ethyl methanoate, so acid part is $\text{HCO-}$ which gives methanoic acid.

**Identify the remaining two esters**

Bottom left is a complex formate ester, $\text{HCOO-R'}$ where R' is a large branched unsaturated alcohol part. The acid part is again $\text{HCO-}$, so this also gives methanoic acid.

Bottom right: $(\text{CH}_{3})_{2}\text{CHCH}_{2}\text{CH}_{2}\text{OCOCH}_{3}$ is 3-methylbutyl ethanoate. The acid part is $\text{CH}_{3}\text{CO-}$, so this gives ethanoic acid.

**Combine to find the distinct acids**

From the four hydrolyses we get: butanoic, methanoic, methanoic again, and ethanoic.

Therefore the organic acids present are butanoic, ethanoic and methanoic acids.

options.A: Incorrect. Butanoic and ethanoic are correct, but propanoic acid is not formed. No ester has a propanoyl group $\text{CH}_{3}\text{CH}_{2}\text{CO-}$. The error is miscounting the butanoate chain or mistaking an ethoxy $\text{-OCH}_{2}\text{CH}_{3}$ alcohol part for a propanoic acid part.
options.B: Correct. Ethyl butanoate gives butanoic acid, 3-methylbutyl ethanoate gives ethanoic acid, and both ethyl methanoate and the complex formate ester give methanoic acid. So only three distinct acids are present.
options.C: Incorrect. This swaps the roles of acid and alcohol. 3-methylbutanoic acid would come from a 3-methylbutanoyl $\text{C=O}$ side, but the bottom right compound has 3-methylbutyl as the alcohol $\text{-O-R'}$ side, giving ethanoic acid, not 3-methylbutanoic acid. Propanoic acid is also not formed.
options.D: Incorrect. Methanoic is correct, but this option makes the same acid-alcohol swap as option C. The bottom right ester gives ethanoic acid from its $\text{CH}_{3}\text{CO-}$ part, not 3-methylbutanoic acid, and no ester gives propanoic acid.
